National Consumer Disputes Redressal
Ireo Grace Realtech Private Limited ... vs Sakshi Abraham And Another on 30 June, 2026
IN THE NATIONAL CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION
 NEW DELHI

 RESERVED ON : 26.05.2026
 PRONOUNCED ON : 30.06.2026

 FIRST APPEAL NO, 257 OF 2025
(Against the orders dated 15.04.2024 and 15.07.2024 in CC No. 205 of 2020 and RA No.
 10/2024 of the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Delhi)

Ireo Grace Realtech Pvt. Ltd.
Registered office at
C-4,1st Floor, Malviya Nagar
Delhi-110017
Through AR Mr. Virender Singh Appellant
 Versus

1. Sakshi Abraham
W/o Mr. Eddy Abraham
2. Eddy Abraham
S/o Mr. K C Abraham
R/o of 142, Akash Neem Marg
DLF Phase-II, Gurgaon-122002, Haryana Respondents

BEFORE:
HON'BLE DR. INDER JIT SINGH, PRESIDING MEMBER
HON'BLE MR. SHASHI NANDKEOLYAR, MEMBER

For the Appellant(s): Ms. Yashika Kapoor, Ms.Ruchi Kumar and
 Mr. Chaitanya Sharma, Advocate

For the Respondent(s): Mr. Aditya Parolia, Ms. Sumbul Ismail, Md. Imran
 Ahmed and Ms. Khushi Singhal, Advocate

 ORDER
DR. INDER JIT SINGH, PRESIDING MEMBER
1. The present First Appeal (FA) has been filed by the Appellant against Respondents
as detailed above, under
section 51
of Consumer Protection Act 2019, against the order
dated 15.04.2024 and 15.07.2024 of the State Consumer Disputes Redressal
Commission Delhi (hereinafter referred to as the 'State Commission"), in Consumer
Complaint (CC) no. 205 of 2020 and RA No. 10 of 2024 in CC No. 205 of 2020
FA/257/2025 Page 1 of 37
respectively, inter alia praying for setting aside the impugned order dated 15.04.2024 in
CC No. 205 of 2020 and order dated 15.07.2024 passed in RA No. 10 of 2024.
2. The Appellant was Opposite Party and the respondents were Complainants before
the State Commission. Both the parties filed their written submissions on 27.05.2026
and 15.04.2026 respectively.
3. Brief facts of the case, as emerged from the FA, Order of the State Commission
and other case records are that in the year 2013, the Complainants booked an
apartment with the Opposite Party in the project "The Corridors" situated at 67 A,
Gurgaon, Haryana. Thereafter, the Opposite Party allotted an Apartment bearing no. CD-
AS-01-102 vide Allotment Letter dated 07.08.2013. Further, an Apartment Buyer
Agreement was executed between the parties vide Agreement dated 25.04.2014. The
Opposite Party assured the complainant that the possession of the said apartment will be
handed over to him within 42 months from the date of approval of the building plans
and/or fulfilment of the preconditions imposed thereunder along with a grace period of 6
months i.e. by January 2017 or even by July, 2017.
4. The complainant claims to have visited office of the opposite party numerous
times to know about the construction of the said project but no satisfactory response
was given by the builder. It is further submitted by the complainant that the last
construction update available on the website of the Opposite Party is of May 2018 which
clearly shows that both the Project and the Apartment were nowhere near completion or
habitable and that the possession could not be delivered by the opposite Party in the
near future. It is further the case of the complainants that despite having collected more
than 2 crores from them, OP has failed to offer possession of the apartment with the
time period promised. The complainants have diligently followed the payment plan and
made all the payments as and when demands were raised by the OP. Further, there is
delay in completing the project and failure to offer possession of the apartment till date
even after the expiry of more than 3 years from the promised date of possession.
Further, the OPs failed to provide any update on completing the project.
5. Aggrieved by this, the Complainants approached the State Commission and State
Commission vide order dated 15.04.2024 allowed the complaint of the complainants with
following directions:
17. Keeping in view the facts of the present case and the extensive
 law as discussed above, we direct the Opposite Party to refund the
 entire amount paid by the Complainants i.e., Rs. 2,13,42,408- along
 with interest as per the following arrangement:
A. An interest @ 6% p.a. calculated from the date on which each
 installment/payment was received by the Opposite Party till
 15.04.2024 (being the date of the presentjudgment);
B. The rate of interest payable as per the aforesaid clause (A) is
 subject to the condition that the Opposite Party
 pays the entire amount on or before 15.06.2024;
FA/257/2025 Page 2 of 37
C Being guided by the principles as discussed above, in case the
 Opposite Parties fails to refund the amount as per
 the aforesaid clause (A) on or before 15.06.2024, the entire amount
 is to be refunded along with an interest®
 9% p.a. calculated from the date on which each
 installment/payment was received by the Opposite Party till the
 actual realization of the amount.
18. In addition to the aforesaid and taking into consideration the
 facts of the present case, the Opposite Party is directed to pay a
 sum of

 A. Rs. 5,00,000/- as cost for mental agony and harassment to the
 Complainants; and
 B. The litigation cost to the extent of Rs. 50,000/-.
6. Being aggrieved of the aforesaid order dated 15.04.2024 of the State Commission,
the OP filed review application no. 10 of 2024 for review of the order dated 15.04.2024
which was also dismissed.
7. The appellant herein, being aggrieved with the order of the State Commission
dated 15.04.2024 as well as order dated 15.07.2024 filed a Petition being CM (M)
3237/2024 and CM Appl. 48976-48978/2024 before the Hon'ble Delhi High Court.
However, the Hon'ble Delhi High Court vide order dated 29.08.2024 observed that
Petitioner can always invoke the jurisdiction of National Commission in terms of
Section
51
and
58
of the Act and disposed of the said petition with liberty to explore the legal
option available to the petitioner. Not satisfied with the order of the Hon'ble High Court
dated 29.08.2024, the Petitioner approached Hon'ble Supreme Court and Hon'ble
Supreme Court vide order dated 06.12.2024 directed the petitioner to deposit a sum of
Rs. 1.00 crore in the Registry of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and subject to deposit of
said amount, there shall be stay of execution proceedings. Again when the matter was
taken up on 20.01.2025, Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that since the petitioner -
Company has a statutory remedy to approach the National Commission, it would not be
proper to adjudicate this matter at this stage.
In the said order dated 20.01.2025,
petitioner submitted that the matter is covered by the judgment of this Court in
Ireo
Grace Realtech Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Sanjay Gopinath
.
8. Therefore, the Appellant is before us now in the present FA.
9. Appellant(s) have challenged the Order of the State Commission mainly on
following grounds:
a. The impugned order dated 15.04.2024 violates the principles of judicial comity
 and propriety, as the State Commission failed to follow the law
laid down by
the
 Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ireo Grace Rea/tech Pvt. Ltd. v. Abhishek Khanna &
 Ors.~ Civil Appeal No. 5785 of 2019
FA/257/2025 Page 3 of 37
b. State Commission failed to follow the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court
 in Abhishek Khanna (supra) whereby it was held that Chart-A/Phase-I allottees (
 as is the respondent in the present case) are obligated to take possession along
 with delay compensation in terms of the Agreement for the period of delay which
 has occurred from 27.11.2018 till the date of offer of possession was made to the
 allottees.
c. State Commission failed to observe that Hon'ble Supreme Court in Abhishek
 Khanna's case nowhere granted refund alongwith interest to chart A allottees of
 the project.
d. State Commission erred in granting refund with interest @6% p.a., contrary to
 the directions in Abhishek Khanna, wherein only delay compensation was
 awarded.
e. Reliance has also been placed on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in
 M/s
Ireo Grace Realtech Pvt. Ltd. v. Sanjay Gopinath Etc.- CA No.
2764-
 2771/2022 dated 28.11.2024, wherein similarly situated Chart-A allottees were
 directed to take possession and were granted delay compensation @ ^7.50 per
 sq. ft. for the period of delay which occurred from 27.11.2018 till the date of offer
 of possession.
f. The construction of the unit stood completed and Notice of Possession was issued
 on 13.06.2019, prior to the filing of the complaint, and therefore not accepting
 the possession of said apartment at such crucial stage would prove highly
 detrimental and prejudicial to the interest of the appellant as well the allottees
 who have already paid full consideration
 g. The Respondents continued making payments, including the final instalment on
10.05.2018, without protest, thereby acknowledging the status of construction
 and terms of the Agreement.
h. The Appellant further submits that revised building plans were communicated to
 the Respondents on 04.08.2016 and no objection was raised by them, indicating
 their satisfaction with the project.
i. From a conjoint reading of Clauses 1, 13.3, 13.4 and 13.5 of the ABA , it is clear
 that that possession was to be offered within 42 months along with 6 months'
 grace period and 12 months' extended period from the date of approval of
 building plans and fulfilment of preconditions.
j. The date of handing over of the possession has to be determined from the date of
 approval of building plans and / or fulfilment of the preconditions imposed
 thereunder, which in the present case would be grant of the fire scheme approval
 on 2.11.2014. Thus, the period of 60 months from 27.11.2014 including 6
 months grace period and 12 months extended delay period will expire only on
 27.11.2019.
k. Respondents filed their complaint prematurely despite the fact that appellant had
 already completed construction and obtained the occupancy certificate for the first
 phase of the project. The appellant issued the notice of possession to the
 respondent on 13.06.2019.
FA/257/2025 Page 4 of 37
I. State Commission failed to appreciate that even though the building approval was
 granted on 27.09.2011, there were several pre-conditions that were required to
 be satisfied before commencement of construction. The NOC regarding fire safety
 was only issued and approved by the concerned authority on 27.11.2014 and
 therefore the proposed period of delivery of possession would be 48 months from
 27.11.2014 i.e. the due date of possession would be 27.11.2018.
 m. The calculation of 42 month period plus an additional 6 months grace period for
 delivering possession of the apartment to the allottees should commence from,
 the date of approval of the building plan and / or the fulfilment of any
 preconditions specified in the contract.
n. The impugned order passed by the State Commission is in the teeth of the
 observations held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in
Bharti Knitting Co. Vs. DHL World
 Wide Courier
1996 4 SCC 704 wherein it was held that parties are bound by the
 terms of the agreement.
10. Heard counsels of both sides. Contentions/pleas of the parties, on various issues
raised in the FA, based on their FA/Reply, Written Arguments, and Oral Arguments
advanced during the hearing, are summed up below:
10.1 Learned counsel for the appellant argued that the dates 27.01.2022 and
 16.02.2022 pertain to Phase-II of the project, and were inadvertently typed in
 place of the correct Phase-I dates Occupation Certificates dated 31.05.2019 and
 Notice of Possession dated 13.06.2019. This error occurred due to the inadvertent
 clerical/typographical oversight arising from the existence of separate phase-wise
 dates recognised in the Abhishek Khanna judgment itself, each having separate
 Occupation Certificates and Notices of Possession. It is also argued that appellant
 had consistently and unequivocally pleaded before the State Commission that
 respondents / complainant's unit formed part of Phase-I of the project whereof
 occupation certificate dated 31.05.2019 had been granted and notice of
 possession dated 13.06.2019 had been issued. Further, the aforesaid inadvertent
 typographical error neither any new plea nor altered the nature and foundation of
 the case.
10.2 The learned counsel for the appellant further submitted that the impugned order
 was contrary to the law
laid down by
the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Abhishek
 Khanna and Sanjay Gopinath. It was argued that the Respondents, being Phase-I
 allottees, were obligated to take possession after issuance of the Occupation
 Certificate and were entitled only to delay compensation for the period of delay.
Therefore, the direction for refund with interest was stated to be contrary to the
 binding decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court. It was also contended that the
 consumer complaint itself was premature since possession had already been
 offered on 13.06.2019, whereas the complaint was filed on 04.09.2020. The
 finding of the State Commission that possession had not been offered was stated
 to be factually incorrect. The Appellant relied upon Clauses 13.4 and 13.5 of the
 Apartment Buyers Agreement (ABA) to submit that the remedy for delayed
 possession was restricted to contractual delay compensation of Rs.7.50 per sq. ft.
FA/257/2025 Page 5 of 37
per month and that the right to seek termination/refund ceased upon issuance of
 the possession notice. Reliance was also placed on
Bharti Knitting Co. v. DHL
 Worldwide Courier
1996 4 SCC 704 to contend that the contractual terms were
 binding on the parties.
10.3 The learned counsel for the appellant further submitted that the delay in
 completion of the project was attributable to force majeure circumstances and
 regulatory impediments, including orders of the National Green Tribunal, delays in
 statutory approvals, and defaults committed by a large number of allottees. In
 terms of Clauses 13.3 and 13.6 of the ABA, such circumstances entitled the
 developer to extension of time for delivery of possession. It was also argued that
 the Respondents themselves had defaulted in payment of a sum of Rs.26,04,813/-
 , and in view of Clause 13.3 of the ABA, a defaulting allottee could not seek
 equitable relief against the developer. The counsel also contended that the relief
 granted by the State Commission was excessive and beyond jurisdiction, as it
 awarded refund, interest and compensation for mental agony, whereas, in terms
 of the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the Respondents were at best
 entitled to delay compensation at the rate of Rs.7.50 per sq. ft. for the period
 from 27.11.2018 till 13.06.2019, subject to adjustment of mutual dues.
10.4. Learned counsel for the respondents argued that this Commission, vide order
 dated 29.05.2025, allowed the condonation of delay application on the basis of
 the Registry's calculation of a delay of 162 days, reckoned from the order dated
 20.01.2025 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court. However, the Registry has
 erred in computing the delay, as the correct calculation ought to have been made
 from the order dated 15.04.2024 passed by the State Commission. The State
 Commission allowed the consumer complaint vide order dated 15.04.2024, and
 the review application filed by the Appellant was disposed of on 15.07.2024. The
 appeal has been filed after a substantial delay of 296 days from the order dated
 15.04.2024 and 205 days from the order dated 15.07.2024. However, in
 IA/6223/2025, the Applicant has stated the delay as only 267 days and 176 days
 respectively, which is factually incorrect and contrary to the record. Despite
 having knowledge of the order dated 15.07.2024 passed by the State Commission
 disposing of the review application, the Appellant did not challenge the same
 within the prescribed period. The appeal was filed only after considerable delay,
 thereby postponing the execution and compliance of the decree passed in favour
 of the Respondents. The Appellant filed Review Application No. RA/10/2024
 challenging the final order passed by the State Commission. Upon considering the
 submissions of the parties and the scope of review jurisdiction under
Section 50
of
 the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the State Commission dismissed the review
 application vide order dated 15.07.2024. The record reflects that, instead of
 availing the statutory appellate remedy, the Appellant challenged the order dated
 15.07.2024 passed in RA/10/2024 by invoking the writ jurisdiction of the Hon'ble
 Delhi High Court in CM(M) 3237/2024 along with connected applications. The
 Hon'ble High Court, vide order dated 29.08.2024, declined to interfere with the
 findings of the State Commission and dismissed the petition. The Appellant
 thereafter challenged the order of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court by filing Special
 Leave Petition (Civil) Diary No. 44527/2024 before the Hon'ble Supreme Court
 under
Article 136
of the Constitution of India. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, vide
FA/257/2025 Page 6 of 37
order dated 20.01.2025, declined to entertain the petition and granted liberty to
 the Appellant to avail the statutory remedy available under the
Consumer
 Protection Act
. The appellant has been resorting to meritless appeals only to
 delay the proceedings. Learned counsel relied on the following judgments :
Ram Lal Vs. Rewa Coalfields Ltd. AIR 1962 SC 361
 ii.
Anshul Aggarwal Vs. NOIDA
2011 14 SCC 578
 iri. Lingeswara Etc. Vs. Thirunagalingam - Special Leave to Appeal ( C)
 Nos.
2054-2055 /2022
 iv.
Pathapati Subba Reddy ( Died) by LRs and Ors. Vs. Special Deputy
 Collector (IA
) 2024 INSC 286

10.5. Learned counsel for the Respondents further contended that the application for
 condonation of delay was allowed without affording them an opportunity to file
 their objections. It is further contended that the delay stated in the application
 was incorrectly computed, and that the condonation of such delay has resulted in
 prolonging the execution proceedings and also gave a scope of hearing a
 hopelessly time barred review application.
10.6. It is also contended by the respondent that State Commission passed a reasoned
 order granting relief to the Respondents on the ground that the Appellant had
 failed to deliver possession within the stipulated period.
In this regard, reliance
 was placed on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in
Newtech
 Promoters & Developers Private Limited v. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors
.
2021 18 SCC 1 wherein it was held that a consumer acquires an unconditional
 right to seek refund where the developer fails to hand over possession within the
 time agreed between the parties.
10.7. It is also argued that the Respondents duly complied with their payment
 obligations under the Agreement. However, owing to the Appellant's failure to
 deliver possession of the unit within the stipulated period, the Respondents
 sought refund of the amounts paid by filing a consumer complaint before the
 State Commission, thereby electing to terminate the contractual arrangement.
 Reliance was placed on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in
Pioneer
 Urban Land & Infrastructure Ltd. v. Geetu Gidwani Verma & Anr
.
11. As regards the objections / contentions of the learned counsel for the respondents
with regard to condonation of delay in filing the First Appeal before this Commission is
concerned, it is to be noted that delay in filing the First Appeal was condoned as per this
Commission's order dated 29.05.2025. Extract of relevant paras of the order dated
29.05.2025 is reproduced below:
1. Respondent is represented by Ms. Ishita Singh who have filed their
 caveat earlier. She takes notice of the appeal execution as well as stay
 application, they are granted four weeks' time
 to file reply to appeal execution as well as stay application in question
 and accordingly, she is discharged as a caveator. The Respondent will
 have four weeks'time to file reply to the Appeal Petition.
FA/257/2025 Page 7 of 37
2. Our attention was drawn to orders of the Hon'ble Supreme Court dated
 20.01.2025, counsel for the Appellants states that in compliance of this
 order they have already deposited the
 requisite amount with Registry of this Commission.
3. Although, as per calculations made by the Registry, the appeal has
 been filed with a delay of 162 days, considering that the matter
 travelled to Hon'ble Supreme Court and orders of the Hon'ble Supreme
 Court are dated 20.01.2025 and the appeal was filed on 07.02.2025
 itself, and delay in filing the appeal is not opposed by the Respondent
 who appeared as caveat, the delay in filing the appeal is condoned and
 it is decided to take up the matter on merits.
4. The counsel for Appellant has also drawn our attention to order dated
 16.12.2024 of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and submitted that in
 addition to the Rs. One crore deposited by them in compliance of this
 order, subsequently on 13.05.2025 they have deposited another
 Rs.1,13,42,218/- with the Registry of this Commission.
XXX XX
12. No doubt period of delay taken in the said order is 162 days, which was
calculated by the Registry as per following details:
Date of cause of action / date of impugned order (SC) 15.04.2024
 Date of Filing 07.02.2025
 Date of order received 30.07.2024
 No. of days taken to file the FA from the date of 298 days
 impugned order / date of cause of action
 Less time taken for obtaining the certified copy 106 days
 Time taken for filing 192 days
 First Appeal filed within time 30 days
 Delay, if any 162 days
13. The impugned order of the State Commission is dated 15.04.2024. Although
Section 51
of Consumer Protection Act, 2019 states that Appeal against the order of
State Commission to National Commission is to be filed within a period of 30 days from
the date of order. As has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in
D. Saibaba v. Bar
Council of India & Ann
, (2003) 6 SCC 186 , the delay is to be counted from the date
of knowledge. Extract of the relevant paras is reproduced below:
FA/257/2025 Page 8 of 37
"lA.How can a person concerned or a person aggrieved be
 expected to exercise the right of review conferred by the provision
 unless the order is communicated to or is known to him either
 actually or constructively? The words "the date of that order",
 therefore, mean and must be construed as meaning the date of
 communication or knowledge, actual or constructive, of the order
 sought to be reviewed."
14. Further Regulations
Regulation 18 (6)
and
Regulation 21
of Consumer Protection (
Consumer Commission Procedure) Regulation 2020, the District Commission / State
Commission, as the case may be is obligated to supply free certified copy of the final
order to all the parties and all subsequent paid certified copies should have details as to
on which date and by what mode free certified copy was supplied. Hence, details of
supply of such free certified copy, including the date of its issue and mode of issue has
to be mentioned on all future paid certified copies. Ideally the appellant should have
placed on record the certified copy of the State Commission's order ( either free or paid)
containing such details, in particular, the date when first free certified copy was issued
and mode of issue of such copy. However, copy of the impugned order placed on record,
though certified as true copy by the Registrar of the State Commission, bears no such
details and this certification of the Registrar is dated 30.07.2024. Hence, in the absence
of relevant / required details, Registry took the date of order receipt as 30.07.2024 and
calculated the delay as 162 days. In the IA No. 6223 of 2025 filed for seeking
condonation of delay, period of delay mentioned by the appellant herein is 267 days. It
is to be noted that when delay was condoned by this Commission vide this Commission's
order dated 29.05.2025, extract of relevant portion of which has been reproduced above,
it was after considering the fact that matter had travelled to Hon'ble Supreme Court and
order of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is dated 20.01.2025 and appeal was filed on
07.02.2025 itself.
Further, order dated 29.05.2025 also records that delay in filing Appeal
was not opposed by the respondent, who appeared as Caveat. However, now again
through its written notes of arguments filed on 15.04.2026, respondent has re-raised the
issue of delay in filing the First Appeal, which has been summed up in para 10.4 of this
order. Although, delay is to be computed from the date of knowledge of the impugned
order, even assuming that delay is to be calculated from the date of impugned order i.e.
15.04.2024, the delay will come to 268 days ( after subtracting statutory permissible
period of 30 days) and if counted from the date of review order i.e. 15.07.2024, the
delay comes to 177 days ( after subtracting statutory period of 30 days). Hence, we are
of the considered view that in the given facts and circumstances of the case and
especially considering the fact that case has travelled to Hon'ble Supreme Court and
order of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is dated 20.01.2025 and appeal was filed on
07.02.2025 itself and in pursuance to the order dated 06.12.2024 and 20.01.2025 of the
Hon'ble Supreme Court, a substantial amount totalling to Rs.2,13,42,408/- has since
been deposited by the appellant herein and keeping in view the various other judgments
of the Hon'ble Supreme Court \ on the issue of condonation of delay, we are of the
considered view that entire delay in filing the present appeal, even if the period is as

1
Collector (LA) v. Katiji
, (
1987) 2 SCC 107, State of Haryana Vs. Chandra Mani
(
1996) 3 SCC 132, N.
Balakrishnan Vs. M. Krishnamurthy
(
1998) 7 SCC 123, Ram Nath Sao Vs. Gobardhan Sao
(
2002) 3 SCC
195, Perumon Bhagvathy Devaswom Vs. Bhargavi Amma
(2008) 8 SCC 321
FA/257/2025 Page 9 of 37
alleged by the respondent, can be condoned and we hereby condone the same.
Moreover, it is to be noted that condonation of delay was not objected to by the learned
counsel for the respondent on 29.05.225, when he / she appeared as Caveat and this is
duly recorded in the order dated 29.05.2025. Hence, the objection of the respondents
with respect to the condonation of delay is hereby rejected.
15. The main contention of the appellant herein is that State Commission has ignored
the law
laid down by
the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Abhishek Khanna. The said case
 pertains to the same project 'The Corridors' developed by the Appellant Builder herein, in
Sector 67-A, Gurgaon, Haryana. In
the said judgment
, Hon'ble Supreme Court
considered at length various issues involved and categorized allottees into 2 broad
categories viz. Chart 'A' allottees of Phase-I which comprised of Tower A6-A10, Bl-B-4
and C-3-C7, wherein occupation certificate was issued on 31.05.2019 and offer of
 possession was made to the apartment buyers and Chart B allottees of Phase-II, with
 respect to Towers in Cluster-A comprising of buildings Al to A5, cluster-B comprising of
 buildings B5 to B8 and Cluster-C comprising of buildings C8 to Cll in which case, the
application for grant of part occupation certificate was submitted on 10.09.2019, which
was pending was approval at that time. Chart A had 3 allottees only while Chart B had
 17 allottees, list of which is given in
the said judgment
. Hon'ble Supreme Court held
that allottees at SI. No.l and 2 in Chart A are obligated to take possession of
the apartments since construction was completed and possession offered on
 28.06.2019, after the issuance of Occupation Certificate on 31.05.2019. The
Court further observed that developer is obligated to pay delay compensation
for the period of delay which occurred from 27.11.2018 till the date of offer of
possession was made to the allottees. A separate directions were given with respect
to the allottee at SI. No. 3 in view of his having filed Civil Appeal under Insolvency and
Bankruptcy Code 2016 before the Hon'ble Supreme Court. As regards allottees in Chart
'B' were concerned, Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that occupation certificate for
towers relating to these allottees have not been obtained yet, holding that allottees in
Chart B are entitled to refund of the entire amount deposited by them. Hon'ble
Supreme Court also took note of the clause 13.4 of the Apartment Buyer's
Agreement which provides that developer shall be liable to pay allottee
compensation calculated @ Rs.7.5 per sq. ft of the super area for every month
of delay, after the end of grace period and held that delay compensation
specified in the Apartment Buyer's Agreement of Rs.7.5 per sq. ft,, which
translates to 0.9% to 1% p.a. on the amount deposited by the Apartment
Buyer cannot be accepted as being adequate compensation for the delay in
construction of the project, observing further that at the same time, we
cannot accept the claim of the apartment buyer for payment of compound
interest © 20% p.a. which has no nexus with the commercial realities of the
prevailing market.
16. Further, with respect to refund, the Hon'ble Court taking note of the prevailing
market conditions as result of Covid-19 Pandemic, which have greatly impacted the
construction industry, observed that it is necessary to balance the competing interest of
both parties, hence ordered refund with interest @ 9% S.I. per annum from 27.11.2018
till the date of payment of the entire amount with a rider that refund be paid within
FA/257/2025 Page 10 of 37
period of three months from the date of judgment and if there is any further delay, the
developer will be liable to pay default interest @ 12% S.I. p.a.
17. As regards committed date of possession, Hon'ble Supreme Court after
considering various aspects held that 42 months period in clause 13.3 of the
agreement for handing over of the possession of the apartment would be
required to be computed from the date on which Fire NOC was issued and not
from the date building plans were sanctioned. No doubt, the building plan
were approved on 23.07.2013, fire NOC was obtained on 27.11.2014, hence
Hon'ble Supreme Court held that commitment period of 42 months plus the
grace period of 6 months from 27.11.2014 would be 27.11.2018, as being the
relevant date for offer of possession. In this case, Hon'ble Supreme Court also
held that apartment buyer cannot be bound by the terms of the agreement
which are oppressive and wholly one-sided as it constitutes unfair trade
practice under the
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
. Extract of relevant portion of
the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court are reproduced below:
1. The present batch of Appeals has been filed by the Appellant-
Developer, to challenge the judgment passed by the National Consumer
 Disputes Redressa! Commission C^tiona! Commission") directing
 refund of the amounts deposited by the Apartment Buyers in the
 project "The Corridors"developed in Sector 67-A, Gurgaon, Haryana, on
 account of the inordinate delay in completing the construction and
 obtaining the Occupation Certificate. Aggrieved by the said Judgment,
 the Appellant-Developer has filed the present batch of Appeals
 under
Section 23
of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 ("
Consumer
 Protection Act
').
